Hi Marissa,

We're starting a GDPR-triggered data export for a European tenant and need clarity on Redwood's capabilities for audit/access logs. Specifically: 
- What retention windows are configurable for tenant audit and access logs (retention min/standard/max)?
- Can you deliver a per-tenant export that includes "tombstone" events (deletion markers) and a manifest with checksums?
- Export formats: NDJSON, CSV, or Parquet? Are streaming/delta exports supported?
- SLA: how long to produce a full export for a 90-day window (~200M events)? Any expected bandwidth limits or staging to S3?
- Proof of deletion: once we request an erase, what evidentiary items can Redwood provide (audit manifest, index of deleted object ids, signed timestamp)?

We're on a legal hold timeline, so any concrete timelines and delivery mechanics would be appreciated. If it's easier, happy to hop on a short call.

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below, plus I attached a short export_spec_template.csv you can fill with the tenant id / date range and preferred delivery option.

Short answers (summary):
- Retention windows: min 30 days, standard 12 months, max configurable up to 7 years for Dedicated/Private customers (policy & billing required).
- Tombstones & manifests: yes — we include tombstone records (deleted flag + deletion timestamp) and generate a manifest containing per-file SHA256 checksums and a top-level index.
- Formats: NDJSON is our default for audit events (line-delimited JSON). We can also deliver Parquet for analytics-friendly ingestion; CSV is supported for small slices.
- Delivery & SLA: typical bulk export SLA is 7 business days for standard requests. For large datasets (200M events) we stage gzipped daily chunks to a customer S3 bucket (signed PUT URLs). Expedited delivery (48–72 hours) is available as a paid option.
- Proof of deletion: we provide an "evidence manifest" (signed by Redwood's export service) listing deleted object ids, tombstone timestamps, and a hash chain anchored to the manifest for tamper-evidence.

Next steps: please populate the attached export_spec_template.csv and indicate whether you want NDJSON or Parquet. Also confirm the S3 bucket destination (or we can provide a signed upload area).

I'll loop Kim (cc'd) for the file-schema and manifest details. If you'd prefer a quick 30-min call we can schedule tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@greenleafhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Audit/access logs export + deletion proof (GDPR/legal hold) — manifest & transport details

Hi Aisha — adding the technical specifics you asked for. I'll keep things concrete so your compliance team can map requirements.

1) Event model + tombstones
- Each audit/access event is a single NDJSON record with fields: event_id, tenant_id, user_id (nullable), action, resource, timestamp, metadata. Deletions are emitted as "tombstone" records where action=\"delete\" and metadata.deleted_object_id is populated. Tombstones are full-fidelity events — they are not retroactive; if an object was deleted before the export window, we include the tombstone if it exists in the retained logs.

2) Manifest & checksums
- For every archive batch (we default to daily slices), we produce: 
  - slice-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz (gzip-compressed NDJSON)
  - slice-YYYYMMDD.ndjson.gz.sha256 (text file of checksum)
  - slice-YYYYMMDD.metadata.json (small JSON manifest; included inline in the evidence_manifest PDF we attach)
- A top-level index.manifest.json lists all slices, their sizes, SHA256 sums, event counts, and a signed ISO8601 timestamp. The signing is HMAC-SHA256 using our export-service key; the signature and key id are in the manifest so you can verify integrity.

3) Delivery mechanics
- Standard path: we stage the slices into a per-tenant export bucket in our EU region, then generate expiring S3 signed URLs (PUT for uploads if you want direct ingest; GET for download). If you prefer, we can push via your SFTP endpoint.
- We support streaming/delta exports: once enabled, we can produce incremental slices (15-min or hourly) for ongoing replication; retention of the export cursor is 30 days by default.

4) SLA & throughput
- 200M events (depending on average event size) is typically 200–350GB compressed. We prefer to deliver as daily gzipped NDJSON tarballs; production SLA 7 business days. If you need faster, expedited 48–72 hour turnaround uses priority jobs and incurs an expedite fee.

5) Proof of deletion / chain of custody
- For erase requests we supply: evidence_manifest.pdf (human-readable) + index.manifest.json (machine-readable) + per-slice checksums. The evidence_manifest describes which object ids were removed and references the tombstone records. We also provide an export-service audit log showing the job id, who requested the erase (email), timestamps, and a signed statement of completion.

6) Legal hold / preservation
- If Greenleaf places a preservation hold, we suspend scheduled deletion for the affected tenant and flag tombstone generation to still emit deletion markers (so you have a full trail). We keep a legal-hold flag in metadata and can export that flag as part of the manifest.

7) Security & encryption
- All slices are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (HTTPS). When we place files into your S3, they are uploaded over a pre-signed, short-lived URL. You can supply KMS CMK details for server-side encryption on your bucket if required.

Operational notes: 
- We recommend NDJSON for compliance exports (easier to inspect, includes tombstones inline). Parquet is great if you plan to run analytics but we lose simple per-line tombstones unless you include a tombstone column.
- We will provide a small sample export (7 days) and the evidence_manifest so your legal team can review before we process the full archive.

I'll attach a sample evidence_manifest PDF and the schema spec (see attachments). Ping me with the tenant id and target date range and we'll queue the sample.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
